checks: Averaging each pointwise inequality under a centered law removes its own multiplier. The positive averaged C permits dividing and gives precisely the displayed interval for c.

With fixed c, the lower inequality gives upper bounds on λ_L from positive moments and lower bounds from negative moments. Each pairwise comparison is exactly the corresponding positive-weight zero-moment test. Zero-moment records impose singleton tests. A finite one-sided list remains feasible, including when no centered law exists.
The upper inequality uses −M_i and (1−γ)V−P_i+cC_i in the same bound argument, independently of λ_L.

In the centered probability polytope, a support of size three or more permits a nonzero two-sided perturbation preserving the two equalities. A two-point extreme support has strictly opposite moments. For a convex combination of centered laws, each interval endpoint is a weighted average of its constituent endpoints with positive coarea reweighting.

For the additional both-sign infinite-index implication in the proof, one index of each sign gives finite bounds on the supremum of lower bounds and infimum of upper bounds, and the pairwise tests put them in order. This requires the already fixed common c and both signs; no all-infinite-index compactness assertion is needed.
The original §3 (2) locator covers the finite equivalence. Its final caution is respected by the explicit hypotheses on the proof's additional infinite-index observation.

overlap.comparison: Its finite-slope obstruction treats a different one-multiplier system with cancellation across orientations. It gives no characterization of the feasible two-multiplier system from centered pair tests.
This supplies another finite obstruction for a common moment multiplier. The present theorem characterizes feasibility when the two multipliers are independent, with a common scalar c only.
